test_set_change: TEST SET EXPANDED: mini-215 -> mini-231. Adds a sixth cuisine bucket, Middle Eastern (N=16), contributed under the standard weighed protocol by collaborators in Amman and Beirut. This is the first half of the Q3 expansion promised in the 2026-07 snapshot; the Sub-Saharan African bucket is still under N=12 and is deliberately NOT published yet. All systems were re-evaluated against the expanded set. IMPORTANT: because the test set changed, the two open-source baselines are NOT bit-identical this snapshot — they were recomputed on mini-231 and moved, which is the expected behaviour of a deterministic control when the set beneath it changes. Their movement is therefore attributable entirely to the harder cuisine mix, and it calibrates how much of each commercial system's drift is set-driven rather than app-driven.

tiers.photo: Photo-based systems evaluated end-to-end on food images.
tiers.manual: Manual-entry apps whose primary input is text search or barcode.

entries.notes: PlateLens photo mode on the expanded mini-231. 10.7% -> 10.6% despite the set growing by 16 meals — the only vendor photo system that improved on the expansion. The new Middle Eastern bucket is its worst cuisine at 13.7%, ahead of South Asian at 13.0%. Top-1 0.931.

Foodvisor photo mode. 16.3% -> 16.2% on the expanded mini-231 — absorbed the new Middle Eastern bucket better than most. The longest sustained single-vendor improvement the benchmark has recorded, concentrated in the South Asian bucket.
Bitesnap photo mode. 14.9% -> 14.8% on the expanded set. Western/Mediterranean unchanged; the new Middle Eastern bucket reads 17.6%.
Calorie Mama photo mode. 15.2% -> 15.1% on the expanded set (the move driven by the new bucket, 17.9%).
Zero-shot over 40 Food-101 labels, 13.8% on mini-231, deterministic. The set grew by 16 meals, so the control moved with it — as it should.
Zero-shot, deterministic, 15.2% on mini-231. See the CLIP note.

PlateLens manual mode. 4.2% -> 4.1% after a database refresh. Small, close to the noise floor, traceable to a specific cause, so recorded. The expanded set that cost the photo tier up to half a point cost this row nothing.
Manual-entry workflow. 4.8% -> 4.9%; the Middle Eastern items exposed a few thin database entries, which is a coverage issue rather than a workflow one.
Manual-entry workflow. 6.6% -> 6.7%. Its NCCDB-aligned database again absorbed a cuisine expansion with the smallest movement in Tier B.
Primary manual / barcode workflow. 9.5% -> 9.6%, within noise.

Manual-entry workflow on the always-free manual log. 11.6% -> 11.7%. Community-submitted entries for the new bucket's items were sparser and more variable, which is the recurring pattern for this database.
